blocks.text:
Design a location-based dating platform like Tinder, where a user swipes through a deck of nearby candidate profiles, and a connection, a match, only forms when both people independently swipe right on each other. Every social platform earlier in this project involved a one-way action, a follow, a like on a post, a comment, visible immediately to everyone. This one is built around the opposite: a one-sided like is never revealed to the other person at all, only a genuinely mutual, two-sided like ever becomes visible to anyone, and getting that guarantee right under real concurrency is the actual hard problem here.

The technique that makes this both correct and comfortable is a conditional mutual-reveal pattern: every swipe is recorded privately, and a match is created, atomically, only at the exact moment a reverse like already exists, so neither person can ever learn about an unreciprocated interest in them.

blocks.text: A user should be shown a deck of nearby candidate profiles they have not yet judged. A user should be able to swipe left, pass, or right, like, on each candidate. A match should be created, and both users notified, only when each has independently swiped right on the other. A profile a user has already swiped on, in either direction, should never appear in their deck again.

blocks.alt: True mutual opt-in, a fast, endless-seeming deck, never repeating an already-judged profile, relevant nearby candidates, and resistance to fake profiles

blocks.text: True mutual opt-in means a one-sided like must never be visible to the other person until they independently like back too, this is the single most important guarantee in the whole design. A fast, endless-seeming deck means the next candidate has to be ready to show instantly, swipe after swipe, with no visible pause. Never repeating an already-judged profile means once a user has swiped left or right on someone, that profile must never resurface for them again. Relevant, nearby candidates means the deck genuinely reflects the user's current location, not an arbitrary or stale one. And resistance to fake profiles means a bot or fabricated profile undermines the entire premise of matching with an actual, real person.

blocks.text: A platform at real scale might have tens of millions of active users, generating billions of swipes per day across the platform. Only a small fraction of right swipes ever become a mutual match, since a match genuinely requires both people to independently feel the same way. A long-time user's own permanent swipe history, the set of every profile they have ever judged, can grow into the thousands over time, and every single deck request has to exclude all of it efficiently.

class DatingService:
    # Tracks one-way right swipes privately, creates a match only when both
    # sides have swiped right on each other, and permanently excludes judged
    # profiles (either direction) from a user's future deck.
    def __init__(self):
        self.right_swipes_by_swiper = {}  # swiperId -> set of who they liked
        self.ever_judged_by_swiper = {}   # swiperId -> everyone they've swiped on, either direction
        self.matched_pair_keys = set()    # canonical "a|b" keys, a < b alphabetically

    def swipe_right(self, swiper_id, target_id):
        self.ever_judged_by_swiper.setdefault(swiper_id, set()).add(target_id)
        self.right_swipes_by_swiper.setdefault(swiper_id, set()).add(target_id)

        target_already_liked_swiper = swiper_id in self.right_swipes_by_swiper.get(target_id, set())

        if target_already_liked_swiper:
            self.matched_pair_keys.add(self._canonical_pair_key(swiper_id, target_id))  # exactly one record, regardless of who swiped last
            return "MATCH"
        return "LIKED_NO_MATCH_YET"  # never visible to the target until they swipe right too

    def swipe_left(self, swiper_id, target_id):
        self.ever_judged_by_swiper.setdefault(swiper_id, set()).add(target_id)  # still permanently excluded going forward

    def match_count(self):
        return len(self.matched_pair_keys)

    def build_deck(self, user_id, candidates):
        judged = self.ever_judged_by_swiper.get(user_id, set())
        return [c for c in candidates if c not in judged]

    def _canonical_pair_key(self, a, b):
        return f"{a}|{b}" if a < b else f"{b}|{a}"  # order-independent, so both directions map to the same key


def main():
    dating = DatingService()

    # Alice swipes right on Bob. Bob has not swiped on Alice yet, so no match forms.
    print("Alice swipes right on Bob:", dating.swipe_right("alice", "bob"))

    # Bob swipes right on Carol. Carol has not swiped on Bob yet, so no match forms.
    print("Bob swipes right on Carol:", dating.swipe_right("bob", "carol"))

    # Bob swipes right on Alice. Alice already swiped right on Bob: a mutual match forms now.
    print("Bob swipes right on Alice:", dating.swipe_right("bob", "alice"))

    # Carol swipes right on Bob. Bob already swiped right on Carol: a mutual match forms now too.
    print("Carol swipes right on Bob:", dating.swipe_right("carol", "bob"))

    print("Total matches created:", dating.match_count())

    # Alice's deck should now exclude Bob, since she already swiped on him.
    alice_candidates = ["bob", "dave", "erin"]
    print("Alice's deck, excluding already-judged profiles:", dating.build_deck("alice", alice_candidates))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

items: Architecture: a geo-partitioned deck service excluding permanently-judged profiles, and a swipe service whose right swipes atomically create a mutual match only when reciprocated.
Capacity: tens of millions of active users, billions of swipes per day, and only a small fraction of right swipes ever becoming a mutual match.
The core techniques: conditional mutual-reveal matching and permanent deck exclusion, both worked through with a real, verified implementation in Java, Python, and C++.
Database: a private, per-user swipe history alongside a pair-keyed match store recording only confirmed, mutual connections.
End-to-end workflows: a one-sided swipe with no visible match yet, and a reciprocal swipe that creates and announces a match, both traced as sequence diagrams.
Consistency: a strongly consistent, atomic match-creation guarantee paired with an eventually consistent, geographically local candidate deck.
Trade-offs: private mutual opt-in versus immediately visible likes versus fully anonymous, unstored browsing, compared directly on privacy and whether a genuine match can ever be detected at all.
